2. Petitioner's case is that he is an officer under Bangladesh Power Development Board that he served as the Resident Engineer equivalent to the post of an Assistant Engineer in charge of electricity supply at Kushtia from March, 1976 to March, 1979, that thereafter he was posted as Executive Engineer on promotion at Patuakhali Distribution Division and served there from March, 1979 to May, 1980; that thereafter he was transferred to Chittagong as Executive Engineer in charge of electric supply, that while at Chittagong he was served with a charge sheet dated 3.9.80 containing thirty-two charges of which sixteen charges related to the period of his service at Kushtia and remaining sixteen charges related to that at Patuakhali, that he showed cause denying all the charges, that the Enquiry Officers found him guilty of misconduct in respect of some of the charges, that by the office order dated 5.10.82 the petitioner was directed to show cause as to why the penalty of dismissal from service should not be imposed on him and that the petitioner showed cause pleading not guilty to the charges alleged to have been proved, but he was dismissed from service with immediate effect by the impugned office order being No. 1258 PDB (E &B)/2A-27/75 dt. 7.12.82 as at Annexure-'C' to the writ petition. 

 3. Petitioner's further case is, that during the pendency of the aforesaid departmental proceeding, he was placed under supension by the office order dated 20.11.82 pending drawl of another departmental proceeding which was although subsequently drawn up but was ultimately dropped in view of the submission of the enquiry report in favour of the petitioner thereafter another departmental proceeding on the basis of a third charge sheet dated 11.8.82 was started against the petitioner and the same continued beyond the knowledge of the petitioner. Ultimately the petitioner was again dismissed from service with retrospective effect from 7.12.82, i.e. the date of the previous order of dismissal from service, vide the impugned office order dated 6.3.84 as at Annexure- 'N' to the writ petition. 

 4. It is also the case of the petitioner that he filed two departmental appeals on 7.12.82 and on 15.5.84 against the first order and the second order of his dismissal from service. During the pendency of the appeals the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 527 in the 1St Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka against both the aforesaid orders of his dismissal from services, that the suit was dismissed for default on 21.5.87 and that thereafter he filed an application against dismissal for non-prosecution on 29.9.85. Thereafter after knowing that his departmental appeal had been dismissed, he filed this writ petition and obtained the present Rule. 

 6. The petitioner has admitted in paragraph 34 of the writ petition that he instituted Title suit No. 527 of 1984 in the 1st Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka against both the orders of his dismissal from service impugned in this writ petition and that subsequently the suit was dismissed for default on 21.5.87. But the petitioner did not disclose under what provision of the Code of Civil Procedure his suit was dismissed. It appears from the copy of the application Annexure-'14' to the supplementary affidavit on behalf of the respondent No. 1 that the petitioner filed the said application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the order of dismissal of this suit and the said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 40 of 1987 which was admittedly dismissed for non-prosecution. Therefore the suit was admittedly dismissed for default under Order 9 rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure. As such, according to Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the petitioner is precluded from instituting a fresh suit as well as a writ petition in respect of same cause of action in view of Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure as hereunder: 

 10. Similar view has been expressed by the Supreme Court of India in the case of SAL Narayan Rowand another Vs. lsbwarlal Bhagwandas and another reported in AIR 1965 (SC) 1818 to the effect that there is no ground for restricting the expression "civil proceeding" only to those proceedings which arise out of civil suits or proceedings which are tried as civil suits, nor is there any rational basis for excluding from its purview proceedings instituted and tried in the High Court in exercise of its writ jurisdiction under the Constitution.
